chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The lowest amount by which Mut'ah (temporary marriage) is permissible is a handful of food, and some of them have reported, a miswak (toothbrush twig).
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal principle of 'qalil' (small amount) for the validity of Mut'ah, emphasizing that the dower need not be substantial to be binding. The inclusion of the miswak as an alternative minimum highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing even modest, everyday items to fulfill the contractual requirement. This reflects the broader Shia view that Mut'ah is a distinct contract where the dower serves as a symbolic guarantee rather than a heavy financial burden.
